A whole Camembert baked in its wooden box with garlic and a few drops of white wine, for dipping new potatoes and gherkins
Pure indulgence, this. As the Camembert bakes, the cheese underneath the crust becomes a hot, creamy, sticky, smelly, bubbling pool.
Take the cheese from its wooden box and remove the paper wrapping. Push the cheese back into the box.

Smear the top of the cheese with the cut halves of garlic. They will lightly scent the cheese without overpowering it (it is actually quite difficult to overpower a Camembert). Make half a dozen tiny holes in the rind and drizzle a little white wine into them. Just a few drops. Replace the lid. Bake in an oven preheated to 200°C/Gas 6 for twenty-five to thirty minutes or until hot and bubbling.
While the cheese is cooking, put the potatoes on to boil in salted water. Serve the melted cheese in its box, dipping in the spuds or some gherkins, or simply a chunk or two of very crusty bread.
